main_section: Symptoms and signs of gastrointestinal diseases
topic: Functional vs organic symptoms; 20% of cancers are GI
candidate: Many GI consultations are for non-organic (functional) symptoms; 20% of all cancers occur in the GI tract, so the clinician's main task is to recognise organic disease among symptoms, signs and investigations. In developing countries malnutrition, infections and parasites add to the picture.
main_coverage: MAIN p2 lists alarm symptoms and says patients with them should be investigated; no statement on functional consultations or cancer proportion (searched: 20%, functional, organic).
reason: Gives the rationale for alarm symptoms; absent from MAIN.
handout_text:
Many GI consultations are for functional (non-organic) symptoms, yet about 20% of all cancers arise in the GI tract.
The clinician's main task is therefore to pick out organic disease; alarm (red-flag) features help do this.

main_section: Symptoms and signs of gastrointestinal diseases
candidate: Vomiting centres are in the reticular formation of the medulla, stimulated by the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and by the vagus; direct stimulation also by drugs, motion sickness and metabolic causes.

handout_text:
The vomiting centres lie in the reticular formation of the medulla.
They are stimulated by the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ) and by the vagus; drugs, motion sickness and metabolic causes can also stimulate these zones directly.

main_section: Symptoms and signs of gastrointestinal diseases
topic: Phases before vomiting: nausea and retching
candidate: Nausea is accompanied by autonomic symptoms (salivation, pallor, sweating); retching is a strong involuntary unproductive effort of vomiting with abdominal muscle contraction.
main_coverage: absent after search for: retching (only mentioned as a trigger of Mallory-Weiss), nausea autonomic, salivation, pallor.
handout_text:
Two phases usually come before vomiting:
Nausea - with autonomic features (salivation, pallor, sweating).
Retching - a strong, involuntary, unproductive effort to vomit with contraction of the abdominal muscles.
